title: MemAgent: Reshaping Long-Context LLM with Multi-Conv RL-based Memory Agent
claim: Baseline models degrade sharply as context length grows, while ours stays nearly flat across orders of magnitude of length.
layout: 1 wide line plot, log-like x-axis, ours highlighted purple on top, legend inside
description: A single wide line chart of score (y-axis, 0 to 80+) against context length in tokens (x-axis, 7K to 3.5M). Two purple lines for the RL-trained memory agent models (14B and 7B) sit at the top, around 70 to 83, and decline only slightly across the full range to 3.5M. Six baseline lines in green, brown and orange (QwenLong-L1, Qwen2.5-Instruct 1M variants, DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen) start at 30 to 75 at short lengths and fall steeply. Most of them reach near zero by about 896K, and they stop at that point. A red dashed vertical line marks truncation near 112K. A legend in the lower right lists all models. The gap between the flat purple lines and the collapsing baselines is what the eye reads first.
caption: Accuracy scores of RULER-HQA [ref] . Even models that employ long-context continual pretraining and extrapolation techniques fail to maintain consistent performance. In contrast, \method with RL only demonstrates marginal performance dropping.
abstract: Despite improvements by length extrapolation, efficient attention and memory modules, handling infinitely long documents with linear complexity without performance degradation during extrapolation remains the ultimate challenge in long-text processing. We directly optimize for long-text tasks in an end-to-end fashion and introduce a novel agent workflow, MemAgent, which reads text in segments and updates the memory using an overwrite strategy. We extend the DAPO algorithm to facilitate training via independent-context multi-conversation generation. MemAgent has demonstrated superb long-context capabilities, being able to extrapolate from an 8K context trained on 32K text to a 3.5M QA task with performance loss < 5% and achieves 95%+ in 512K RULER test.
